content: Common animation-timing mistake in browser robot simulators: interpolating linearly between two joint configurations (joint-space lerp) and assuming the end-effector traces a straight line in task space -- it does not; joint-space interpolation produces curved, unpredictable task-space paths. For linear g-code moves (G1) the correct approach is to interpolate the TCP pose in Cartesian/task space (position + orientation) and solve IK at each sampled point, not to lerp joint angles directly. Forward kinematics is cheap and used for real-time rendering; inverse kinematics is the expensive/error-prone part and must be solved per waypoint for accurate playback, not just at segment endpoints.
